# Runbook

> A field manual for troubleshooting: how to work out what is wrong, what to do first, and what to do when you are blocked

- Live: https://runbook.neorgon.com/
- Part of the Neorgon tool suite (free, no signup, runs in your browser): https://neorgon.com/
- Keywords: troubleshooting, debugging, incident response, on-call, root cause analysis, escalation

## What it covers

Method rather than any single technology. Nine chapters plus a failure-mode
reference, each section deep-linkable as https://runbook.neorgon.com/#<section-id>.

- 1. Reacting to a Problem: triage questions, scope and blast radius, the four usual suspects, status updates for leadership
- 2. Preemptive Strategies: negative thinking, bounds set while rested, questions to answer while calm, the escalation ladder
- 3. Quick Methods: time correlation, reproduction, differential comparison, reading errors, one variable at a time, searching well
- 4. Long Methods: bisection, mocking and substitution, ruling out in writing, the scientific method, instrumenting instead of guessing
- 5. Understanding Is Half the Battle: notes as a debugging tool, drawing the request path, rubber duck debugging, naming assumptions
- 6. Proper Escalation: checklists for infrastructure, development, dependencies, and everything else, plus how to hand off
- 7. Plan B: restore before you understand, rollback, kill switches, graceful degradation, asking for help, stopping
- 8. Experience and Sharing: pattern recognition, writing runbooks, blameless post-mortems, not being a single point of failure
- 9. The Classics: cache, DNS, certificate expiry, IAM changes, works-in-development, never-exercised code paths
- A. Failure-Mode Reference: twelve common alerts with signal, first moves, and the usual misdiagnosis
